name: The example
expr: (lambda c: (lambda r: [sorted(r) == sorted(c), all(isinstance(x, str) and x != '' and set(x) <= {'0', '1'} for x in r.values()), (lambda s: all(not s[k + 1].startswith(s[k]) for k in range(len(s) - 1)))(sorted(r.values())), sum(c[k] * len(r[k]) for k in c)])(huffman(dict(c))))(args[0])
show: huffman({'a': 5, 'b': 9, 'c': 12, 'd': 13, 'e': 16, 'f': 45}): [same letters?, all codes made of 0 and 1?, no code starts another?, total bits]
why: 224 bits, as in the lesson. Any codes with this total are accepted; equal weights can give different trees.

show: huffman({'x': 3, 'y': 100}): [same letters?, all codes made of 0 and 1?, no code starts another?, total bits]

name: One letter
expr: (lambda c: (lambda r: [sorted(r) == sorted(c), all(isinstance(x, str) and x != '' and set(x) <= {'0', '1'} for x in r.values()), (lambda s: all(not s[k + 1].startswith(s[k]) for k in range(len(s) - 1)))(sorted(r.values())), sum(c[k] * len(r[k]) for k in c)])(huffman(dict(c))))(args[0])
show: huffman({'z': 7}): [same letters?, all codes made of 0 and 1?, no code starts another?, total bits]
why: 7: a single letter still needs a code of at least one bit. Give it '0' (an empty code fails).

name: All equal
expr: (lambda c: (lambda r: [sorted(r) == sorted(c), all(isinstance(x, str) and x != '' and set(x) <= {'0', '1'} for x in r.values()), (lambda s: all(not s[k + 1].startswith(s[k]) for k in range(len(s) - 1)))(sorted(r.values())), sum(c[k] * len(r[k]) for k in c)])(huffman(dict(c))))(args[0])
show: huffman(8 letters, each once): [same letters?, all codes made of 0 and 1?, no code starts another?, total bits]
why: 24: eight letters with equal counts get 3 bits each.

name: Doubling counts
expr: (lambda c: (lambda r: [sorted(r) == sorted(c), all(isinstance(x, str) and x != '' and set(x) <= {'0', '1'} for x in r.values()), (lambda s: all(not s[k + 1].startswith(s[k]) for k in range(len(s) - 1)))(sorted(r.values())), sum(c[k] * len(r[k]) for k in c)])(huffman(dict(c))))(args[0])
show: huffman({'a': 1, 'b': 1, 'c': 2, 'd': 4, 'e': 8, 'f': 16, 'g': 32}): [same letters?, all codes made of 0 and 1?, no code starts another?, total bits]
why: 126: each new tree is lighter than the next letter, so the tree is a long path and a gets 6 bits.

name: Codes must not start each other
expr: (lambda c: (lambda r: [sorted(r) == sorted(c), all(isinstance(x, str) and x != '' and set(x) <= {'0', '1'} for x in r.values()), (lambda s: all(not s[k + 1].startswith(s[k]) for k in range(len(s) - 1)))(sorted(r.values())), sum(c[k] * len(r[k]) for k in c)])(huffman(dict(c))))(args[0])
show: huffman({'a': 10, 'b': 10, 'c': 1, 'd': 1, 'e': 1}): [same letters?, all codes made of 0 and 1?, no code starts another?, total bits]
why: If one code is the start of another (say '1' and '10'), the bits cannot be read back. Read the codes off the leaves of one tree.

name: Words as letters
expr: (lambda c: (lambda r: [sorted(r) == sorted(c), all(isinstance(x, str) and x != '' and set(x) <= {'0', '1'} for x in r.values()), (lambda s: all(not s[k + 1].startswith(s[k]) for k in range(len(s) - 1)))(sorted(r.values())), sum(c[k] * len(r[k]) for k in c)])(huffman(dict(c))))(args[0])
show: huffman({'the': 50, 'cat': 7, 'sat': 7, 'on': 20, 'mat': 3, 'a': 13}): [same letters?, all codes made of 0 and 1?, no code starts another?, total bits]
why: The keys can be any strings. Keep them apart from the trees in the heap: compare by weight, then by a counter.

name: 50,000 letters
args: ({f'w{k}': x for k, x in enumerate([(k * 7919 + 13) % 100000 + 1 for k in range(50000)])},)
expr: (lambda c: (lambda r: [sorted(r) == sorted(c), all(isinstance(x, str) and x != '' and set(x) <= {'0', '1'} for x in r.values()), (lambda s: all(not s[k + 1].startswith(s[k]) for k in range(len(s) - 1)))(sorted(r.values())), sum(c[k] * len(r[k]) for k in c)])(huffman(dict(c))))(args[0])
show: 50,000 different letters with counts up to 100,000: [same letters?, all codes made of 0 and 1?, no code starts another?, total bits]
why: Use a heap: O(k log k). Sorting the list again after every join, or scanning it for the two smallest, costs O(k) or more per join.
